newsitem.title: USA: Tropical depression stalls in Gulf of Mexico.
newsitem.headline: Tropical depression stalls in Gulf of Mexico.

text.p: The 10th tropical depression of the Atlantic hurricane season stalled in the Gulf of Mexico on Saturday but still might strenghten to a tropical storm, the National Hurricane Center said.
At 11 a.m. EDT (1500 GMT) there was "no big change," forecaster Lixion Avila said.
"Same position, same intensity and stationary," he said, adding: "It might still become a tropical storm.

Tropical Depression number 10 was lying 200 miles (320 km) south-southeast of Brownsville, Texas, at latitude 23.0 north and longitude 96.3 west. The storm's location also put it about 65 miles (110 km) east-northeast of Tampico, Mexico.
Maximum sustained winds were near 35 mph (55 kph).
Tropical depressions become tropical storms and are given names when maximum winds reach 39 mph (62 kph) and gain hurricane status when winds hit 74 mph (119 kph).
The depression would be named Josephine if it strengthened into a tropical storm.
